narrative.text:
I’ll run the machinery audit before any other Git command, then read LOW-1 and verify the branch and recovery refs. I’ll keep the fix limited to suppressing reply preparation for the trusted applied context-only plan, add test source without running it, and create a new commit.The audit found no executable machinery or applicable attributes, and the three required named refs match. The worktree initially had the dispatch branch checked out; I switched to the verified composition branch and added the merge recovery ref.

I’m passing the validated plan through the internal admission call to the reply-preparation condition. A’s admission and D’s pre/post checks remain in place; absent or conversational plans retain the existing reply path.The source change is in place, and the new test source covers context-only acceptance, both mixed-batch orders, negative/stale admission, post-hook grant narrowing, and normal delivery despite a false wake gate. It also checks that forged wire or metadata hints cannot suppress preparation without an applied plan. I’m reviewing the diff and unchanged checks before committing; no tests will run.The fix is committed as `b05df842`, followed by the one-line test-typing commit `54ebfc58`; neither has a co-author trailer. Fresh source-only gates passed at `54ebfc58`: whitespace, protected-module equality, reachability of the original merge and both parents, and tracked-tree cleanliness.

The report contains the diff citations, assertion names, mutant descriptions, audit, and command chronology. No build/test run; runtime behavior and type correctness remain unverified.
